children: is set to release its fiscal Q1 earnings report on Thursday after the market closes, and options traders are positioning for a double-digit post-earnings price swing. Shares of the software giant closed Tuesday's session at $162.52, climbing 2.4%, as market participants solidified their bets ahead of the release.
Based on the at-the-money straddle pricing for the

, the market is implying a post-earnings move of roughly 12% in either direction. The $162.50 strike calls closed near $9.53, while the corresponding puts were priced around $9.46. This combined premium suggests traders are bracing for the stock to swing by roughly $19 by the end of the week, establishing an implied trading range broadly between $143 and $181 following the quarterly report.

A closer look at the open interest positioning reveals a distinct bullish skew among market participants. Call options heavily outweigh put positioning across key strikes, signaling that speculators are primarily targeting upside breakouts.

The $175 strike call stands out with a massive open interest of over 12.6K contracts, acting as a major upside target and potential resistance level. Additionally, heavy call open interest at the $200 strike indicates aggressive upside bets on a highly favorable earnings surprise.

Conversely, put open interest remains relatively muted. Deep out-of-the-money puts show minimal volume in the early strikes, while the largest put concentrations sit at the $150 and $140 strikes. Furthermore, deep in-the-money put contracts reflect relatively thin trading volume compared with the out-of-the-money calls. Even the deep in-the-money calls maintain steady open interest but pale in comparison with the speculative near-the-money upside bets.
This disparity in positioning suggests that while heightened volatility is expected, the overarching sentiment leading into Thursday's print leans heavily optimistic.

title: Oracle earnings: Options traders eye $175 strike on heavy call bias
